# 2450     "\n",

# 3346     "\n",
# 3347     "#  Step 2: Extract real prompt and response from JSON\n",
# 3348     "def extract_prompt_response(row):\n",
# 3349     "    try:\n",
# 3350     "        input_data = json.loads(row[\"input\"]) if isinstance(row[\"input\"], str) else {}\n",
# 3351     "        output_data = json.loads(row[\"output\"]) if isinstance(row[\"output\"], str) else {}\n",
# 3352     "\n",
# 3353     "        prompt_text = input_data.get(\"prompt\", {}).get(\"prompt\", \"\")\n",
# 3354     "        response_text = output_data.get(\"response\", \"\")\n",
# 3355     "\n",
# 3356     "        return pd.Series({\n",
# 3357     "            \"input_text\": prompt_text,\n",
# 3358     "            \"output_text\": response_text\n",
# 3359     "        })\n",
# 3360     "    except Exception:\n",
# 3361     "        return pd.Series({\"input_text\": \"\", \"output_text\": \"\"})\n",
# 3362     "\n",
# 3363     "#  Apply extraction\n",
# 3364     "df_cost[[\"input_text\", \"output_text\"]] = df_cost.apply(extract_prompt_response, axis=1)\n",
# 3365     "\n",
# 3366     "#  Step 3: Estimate tokens from words (input + output)\n",
# 3367     "df_cost[\"input_words\"] = df_cost[\"input_text\"].str.split().apply(len)\n",
# 3368     "df_cost[\"output_words\"] = df_cost[\"output_text\"].str.split().apply(len)\n",
# 3369     "df_cost[\"total_words\"] = df_cost[\"input_words\"] + df_cost[\"output_words\"]\n",
# 3370     "df_cost[\"approx_tokens\"] = df_cost[\"total_words\"] * 1.4  #  conservative multiplier\n",
# 3371     "\n",
# 3372     "#  Step 4: Map provider → model and token cost\n",
# 3373     "provider_id_to_model = {\n",
# 3374     "    1: \"mock-llm\",\n",
# 3375     "    2: \"gpt-4o\",\n",
# 3376     "    3: \"gemini-1.5-pro\",\n",
# 3377     "    4: \"claude-3-sonnet\",\n",
# 3378     "}\n",
# 3379     "cost_map = {\n",
# 3380     "    \"mock-llm\": 0.0,\n",
# 3381     "    \"gpt-4o\": 0.005,\n",
# 3382     "    \"gemini-1.5-pro\": 0.007,\n",
# 3383     "    \"claude-3-sonnet\": 0.003,\n",
# 3384     "}\n",
# 3385     "\n",
# 3386     "df_cost[\"model\"] = df_cost[\"provider_id\"].map(provider_id_to_model)\n",
# 3387     "df_cost[\"cost_per_1k_tokens\"] = df_cost[\"model\"].map(cost_map)\n",
# 3388     "df_cost[\"estimated_cost\"] = (df_cost[\"approx_tokens\"] / 1000) * df_cost[\"cost_per_1k_tokens\"]\n",
# 3389     "\n",
# 3390     "#  Step 5: Summarize by model\n",
# 3391     "#  Step 5: Summarize by model, including token count\n",
# 3392     "summary = (\n",
# 3393     "    df_cost\n",
# 3394     "    .dropna(subset=[\"estimated_cost\", \"model\"])\n",

# 7391     "#  Step 1: Copy and prep\n",

# 7395     "    2: \"gpt-4o\",\n",
# 7396     "    3: \"gemini-1.5-pro\",\n",
# 7397     "    4: \"claude-3-sonnet\",\n",
# 7398     "})\n",
# 7399     "\n",
# 7400     "#  Step 2: Extract prompt/response and estimate cost\n",
# 7401     "def extract_text_lengths(row):\n",
# 7402     "    try:\n",
# 7403     "        input_data = json.loads(row[\"input\"]) if isinstance(row[\"input\"], str) else {}\n",
# 7404     "        output_data = json.loads(row[\"output\"]) if isinstance(row[\"output\"], str) else {}\n",
# 7405     "        prompt = input_data.get(\"prompt\", {}).get(\"prompt\", \"\")\n",
# 7406     "        response = output_data.get(\"response\", \"\")\n",
# 7407     "        return pd.Series({\n",
# 7408     "            \"input_words\": len(prompt.split()),\n",
# 7409     "            \"output_words\": len(response.split())\n",
# 7410     "        })\n",
# 7411     "    except Exception:\n",
# 7412     "        return pd.Series({\"input_words\": 0, \"output_words\": 0})\n",
# 7413     "\n",

# 7415     "df_efficiency[\"approx_tokens\"] = (df_efficiency[\"input_words\"] + df_efficiency[\"output_words\"]) * 1.4\n",
# 7416     "\n",

# 7418     "cost_map = {\n",

# 9304     "})\n",
# 9305     "\n",

# 9310     "        return sum(1 for line in lines if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith(\"# \"))\n",
# 9311     "    except:\n",
# 9312     "        return 0\n",
# 9313     "\n",
# 9314     "df_stmt[\"statement_count\"] = df_stmt[\"response\"].fillna(\"\").apply(count_statements)\n",

# 10354     "    except:\n",
# 10355     "        return 0\n",
# 10356     "\n",
# 10357     "df_corr[\"statement_count\"] = df_corr[\"response\"].fillna(\"\").apply(count_statements)\n",

# 15332     "import re\n",
# 15333     "\n",
# 15334     "#  Step 1: Copy and extract\n",
# 15335     "df_percent = df_engine_expanded.copy()\n",
# 15336     "\n",
# 15337     "def extract_code_pair(row):\n",
# 15338     "    try:\n",
# 15339     "        input_data = json.loads(row[\"input\"]) if isinstance(row[\"input\"], str) else {}\n",
# 15340     "        prompt_block = input_data.get(\"prompt\", {})\n",
# 15341     "        prompt_text = prompt_block.get(\"prompt\", \"\")\n",
# 15342     "\n",
# 15343     "        match = re.search(r'\"source_code\"\\s*:\\s*\"((?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*)\"', prompt_text)\n",
# 15344     "        before = match.group(1) if match else \"\"\n",
# 15345     "\n",
# 15346     "        output_data = json.loads(row[\"output\"]) if isinstance(row[\"output\"], str) else {}\n",
# 15347     "        after = output_data.get(\"response\", \"\")\n",
# 15348     "        if \"[CODE]\" in after and \"[/CODE]\" in after:\n",
# 15349     "            after = after.split(\"[CODE]\", 1)[1].split(\"[/CODE]\", 1)[0].strip()\n",
# 15350     "\n",
# 15351     "        return pd.Series({\n",
# 15352     "            \"before_code\": before.strip(),\n",
# 15353     "            \"after_code\": after.strip()\n",
# 15354     "        })\n",
# 15355     "    except Exception:\n",
# 15356     "        return pd.Series({\"before_code\": \"\", \"after_code\": \"\"})\n",
# 15357     "\n",
# 15358     "df_percent[[\"before_code\", \"after_code\"]] = df_percent.apply(extract_code_pair, axis=1)\n",
# 15359     "\n",
# 15360     "#  Step 2: Levenshtein + percent change\n",
# 15361     "df_percent[\"code_diff\"] = df_percent.apply(\n",
# 15362     "    lambda row: levenshtein_distance(row[\"before_code\"], row[\"after_code\"]),\n",
# 15363     "    axis=1\n",
# 15364     ")\n",
# 15365     "df_percent[\"before_len\"] = df_percent[\"before_code\"].str.len().clip(lower=1)  #  avoid division by 0\n",
# 15366     "df_percent[\"percent_change\"] = (df_percent[\"code_diff\"] / df_percent[\"before_len\"]) * 100\n",
# 15367     "\n",
# 15368     "#  Step 3: Filter and label\n",
# 15369     "df_percent = df_percent[df_percent[\"percent_change\"] > 0].copy()\n",

# 1139     "# # #  ⏱️ Tool Invocation Frequency (Grouped by 60-Second Intervals)\n",
# 1140     "\n",
# 1141     "This cell visualizes **how frequently each tool is invoked over time**, grouped into 60-second bins. It provides a timeline-style view of tool activity, helping identify bursts, patterns, or idle periods during execution.\n",
# 1142     "\n",
# 1143     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 1144     "\n",
# 1145     "* **Binning**:\n",
# 1146     "\n",
# 1147     "  * Floors each tool execution timestamp into 60-second intervals (`time_bin`) for time-based grouping.\n",
# 1148     "\n",
# 1149     "* **Aggregation**:\n",
# 1150     "\n",
# 1151     "  * Groups by both `tool_name` and `time_bin`, counting how many times each tool is called per interval.\n",
# 1152     "\n",
# 1153     "* **Plotting**:\n",
# 1154     "\n",
# 1155     "  * Uses a grouped bar chart to display each tool’s invocation count in each 60-second window.\n",
# 1156     "  * Bars are color-coded by tool for easy comparison.\n",
# 1157     "  * Adds numeric annotations above each bar (`text_auto=True`).\n",
# 1158     "\n",
# 1159     "# # # #  🔍 What you're observing:\n",
# 1160     "\n",
# 1161     "* This plot reveals **temporal distribution of tool usage**:\n",
# 1162     "\n",
# 1163     "  * Tools invoked in bursts will show **tall bars concentrated in narrow windows**.\n",
# 1164     "  * Regular, consistent usage will appear more evenly distributed.\n",
# 1165     "* Great for validating:\n",
# 1166     "\n",
# 1167     "  * **Concurrent execution** patterns\n",
# 1168     "  * **Performance bottlenecks**\n",
# 1169     "  * **Tool scheduling balance**\n",
# 1170     "\n",
# 1171     "This is especially useful as you scale into larger datasets, where **temporal structure** of tool usage becomes a key factor in optimization and traceability.\n"
# 1172    ]

# 1181     "#  1. Floor timestamps to 60-second bins\n",

# 1183     "\n",

# 1191     "\n",

# 3037     "import plotly.graph_objects as go\n",
# 3038     "from app.enums.tool_enums import ToolProvider\n",
# 3039     "\n",
# 3040     "#  Step 1: Prep\n",
# 3041     "df_tool_expanded['tool_name'] = df_tool_expanded['provider_id'].apply(ToolProvider.get_name)\n",
# 3042     "df_tool_expanded['timestamp'] = pd.to_datetime(df_tool_expanded['timestamp'])\n",
# 3043     "\n",
# 3044     "#  Step 2: Assign numeric x positions to categories\n",
# 3045     "tool_names = sorted(df_tool_expanded['tool_name'].unique())\n",
# 3046     "tool_to_num = {tool: i for i, tool in enumerate(tool_names)}\n",
# 3047     "df_tool_expanded['x_numeric'] = df_tool_expanded['tool_name'].map(tool_to_num)\n",
# 3048     "\n",
# 3049     "#  Step 3: Add jitter to numeric x\n",
# 3050     "jitter_strength = 0.25\n",
# 3051     "df_tool_expanded['x_jittered'] = df_tool_expanded['x_numeric'] + np.random.uniform(-jitter_strength, jitter_strength, size=len(df_tool_expanded))\n",
# 3052     "\n",
# 3053     "#  Step 4: Create traces\n",
# 3054     "box_traces = []\n",
# 3055     "for tool, x_val in tool_to_num.items():\n",
# 3056     "    box_traces.append(go.Box(\n",
# 3057     "        y=df_tool_expanded[df_tool_expanded['tool_name'] == tool]['latency_ms'],\n",
# 3058     "        x=[x_val] * len(df_tool_expanded[df_tool_expanded['tool_name'] == tool]),\n",
# 3059     "        name=tool,\n",
# 3060     "        boxpoints=False,\n",
# 3061     "        fillcolor='rgba(120, 81, 169, 0.25)',  #  soft violet fill\n",
# 3062     "        line_color='rgba(80, 50, 120, 0.9)',   #  strong edge\n",
# 3063     "        marker_color='rgba(80, 50, 120, 0.9)',\n",
# 3064     "        width=0.5,\n",
# 3065     "        showlegend=False\n",
# 3066     "    ))\n",
# 3067     "\n",
# 3068     "scatter_trace = go.Scatter(\n",
# 3069     "    x=df_tool_expanded['x_jittered'],\n",
# 3070     "    y=df_tool_expanded['latency_ms'],\n",
# 3071     "    mode='markers',\n",
# 3072     "    marker=dict(\n",
# 3073     "        color='rgba(120, 81, 169, 0.4)',  #  softened violet, translucent\n",

# 3076     "    hoverinfo='skip',\n",
# 3077     "    showlegend=False\n",
# 3078     ")\n",
# 3079     "\n",
# 3080     "#  Step 5: Build figure\n",
# 3081     "fig = go.Figure(data=box_traces + [scatter_trace])\n",

# 5134     "from app.enums.tool_enums import ToolProvider\n",
# 5135     "\n",
# 5136     "#  Ensure tool_name column exists\n",
# 5137     "df_tool_expanded['tool_name'] = df_tool_expanded['provider_id'].apply(ToolProvider.get_name)\n",
# 5138     "\n",
# 5139     "#  1) Compute violation count per row\n",
# 5140     "def count_violations(v):\n",
# 5141     "    try:\n",
# 5142     "        if isinstance(v, str):\n",
# 5143     "            return len(json.loads(v))\n",
# 5144     "        elif isinstance(v, list):\n",
# 5145     "            return len(v)\n",
# 5146     "    except Exception:\n",
# 5147     "        return 0\n",
# 5148     "    return 0\n",
# 5149     "\n",
# 5150     "df_tool_expanded['violation_count'] = df_tool_expanded['violations'].apply(count_violations)\n",
# 5151     "\n",
# 5152     "#  2) Compute average violations per tool per run\n",
# 5153     "if 'run_id' in df_tool_expanded.columns:\n",
# 5154     "    run_tool = (\n",
# 5155     "        df_tool_expanded\n",
# 5156     "        .groupby(['run_id', 'tool_name'])['violation_count']\n",
# 5157     "        .sum()\n",
# 5158     "        .reset_index()\n",
# 5159     "    )\n",
# 5160     "    avg_violations = (\n",
# 5161     "        run_tool\n",
# 5162     "        .groupby('tool_name')['violation_count']\n",
# 5163     "        .mean()\n",
# 5164     "        .sort_values()\n",
# 5165     "    )\n",
# 5166     "else:\n",
# 5167     "    avg_violations = (\n",

# 5170     "        .mean()\n",
# 5171     "        .sort_values()\n",
# 5172     "    )\n",
# 5173     "\n",
# 5174     "avg_df = avg_violations.reset_index()\n",
# 5175     "avg_df.columns = ['tool_name', 'avg_violations']\n",

# 318     "# # #  📦 Treemap of Provider Execution Cost\n",
# 319     "\n",
# 320     "This chart presents a **latency-weighted treemap** that reveals the **nested execution structure** of a CodeCritic run — from top-level orchestration down to fine-grained tooling.\n",
# 321     "\n",
# 322     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 323     "- **Builds a call hierarchy** by tracing each provider’s `called_by_type`, recursively reconstructing the execution path for every log entry.\n",
# 324     "- **Flattens each path** into separate columns (e.g., `path_0`, `path_1`, ...) so Plotly can visualize the full call stack as a nested tree.\n",
# 325     "- **Visualizes latency cost** using a treemap, where:\n",
# 326     "  - Each **box** represents a provider type at a specific nesting level.\n",
# 327     "  - **Box size** is proportional to total `latency_ms` contributed by that node and its descendants.\n",
# 328     "  - **Color** corresponds to `provider_type`, using a colorblind-safe palette.\n",
# 329     "\n",
# 330     "# # # #  🔍 What you're observing:\n",
# 331     "- The **upper-left boxes** show top-level orchestrators (e.g., `session`, `program`).\n",
# 332     "- As you move inward (right and down), you see **nested calls** to `controller`, `system`, `state`, and ultimately `agent`, `tool`, `score`, etc.\n",
# 333     "- **Larger boxes** deeper in the tree indicate subsystems that consume significant time (e.g., tools like `mypy`, `black`, `ruff`).\n",
# 334     "- Hovering on a box reveals its exact path and latency.\n",
# 335     "\n",
# 336     "This visualization is ideal for:\n",
# 337     "- Identifying where latency accumulates in multi-step workflows.\n",
# 338     "- Spotting repeated or redundant calls.\n",
# 339     "- Auditing nested delegation patterns during FSM-driven execution.\n"
# 340    ]
# 341   },
# 342   {
# 343    "cell_type": "code",
# 344    "execution_count": null,
# 345    "id": "2cbc99c8",
# 346    "metadata": {},
# 347    "outputs": [],
# 348    "source": [
# 349     "import plotly.express as px\n",
# 350     "import pandas as pd\n",
# 351     "\n",
# 352     "#  Non-destructive copy\n",
# 353     "df_treemap = df.copy()\n",
# 354     "\n",
# 355     "#  Truncate provider_type\n",
# 356     "df_treemap[\"provider_label\"] = df_treemap[\"provider_type\"].astype(str).str.split(\".\").str[-1]\n",
# 357     "df_treemap[\"source\"] = df_treemap[\"called_by_type\"].fillna(\"root\")\n",
# 358     "df_treemap[\"target\"] = df_treemap[\"provider_label\"]  #  simplified target\n",
# 359     "\n",
# 360     "#  Edge list from simplified names\n",
# 361     "edges = list(zip(df_treemap[\"source\"], df_treemap[\"target\"]))\n",
# 362     "\n",
# 363     "#  Recursive path builder\n",
# 364     "def build_path(row, edges):\n",
# 365     "    if row[\"source\"] == \"root\":\n",
# 366     "        return [\"root\", row[\"target\"]]\n",
# 367     "    for src, tgt in edges:\n",
# 368     "        if tgt == row[\"source\"]:\n",
# 369     "            return build_path({\"source\": src, \"target\": tgt}, edges) + [row[\"target\"]]\n",
# 370     "    return [\"root\", row[\"source\"], row[\"target\"]]\n",
# 371     "\n",
# 372     "#  Build full hierarchical path\n",
# 373     "df_treemap[\"call_path\"] = df_treemap.apply(lambda row: build_path(row, edges), axis=1)\n",
# 374     "\n",
# 375     "#  Flatten and clean hierarchy\n",
# 376     "path_df = df_treemap[\"call_path\"].apply(pd.Series)\n",
# 377     "path_df.columns = [f\"path_{i}\" for i in path_df.columns]\n",
# 378     "\n",
# 379     "#  Add final disambiguator for leaf nodes\n",
# 380     "path_df[path_df.columns[-1]] = df_treemap.apply(\n",
# 381     "    lambda row: f\"{row['provider_label']} (ID {row['provider_id']})\", axis=1\n",
# 382     ")\n",
# 383     "\n",
# 384     "#  Ensure numeric latency\n",
# 385     "df_treemap[\"latency_ms\"] = pd.to_numeric(df_treemap[\"latency_ms\"], errors=\"coerce\").fillna(0)\n",
# 386     "\n",
# 387     "#  Combine everything\n",
# 388     "sunburst_data = pd.concat([df_treemap, path_df], axis=1)\n",
# 389     "\n",
# 390     "#  Plot\n",
# 391     "fig = px.treemap(\n",
# 392     "    sunburst_data,\n",
# 393     "    path=path_df.columns.tolist(),\n",
# 394     "    values=\"latency_ms\",\n",
# 395     "    color=\"provider_label\",\n",
# 396     "    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Safe,\n",
# 397     "    title=\"📦 Treemap of Provider Execution Cost\"\n",
# 398     ")\n",
# 399     "\n",
# 400     "fig.update_traces(root_color=\"lightblue\")\n",
# 401     "fig.show()\n"
# 402    ]
# 403   },

# 409     "# # #  🧩 Execution Flow (Provider Type Nesting)\n",
# 410     "\n",
# 411     "This Sankey diagram visualizes the hierarchical execution path taken by the system during a program run.\n",
# 412     "\n",
# 413     "# # # #  🔍 What this code does:\n",
# 414     "- The code groups log entries (`provider_log`) by their `called_by_type` (who invoked them) and `provider_type` (what kind of provider was called).\n",
# 415     "- It then builds a flow network showing how control moves from one provider type to the next.\n",
# 416     "- The width of each band represents the number of calls made along that path.\n",
# 417     "\n",
# 418     "# # # #  🧠 What you're seeing in the chart:\n",
# 419     "- **Left-to-right flow** from high-level providers like `session`, `program`, and `controller`, down to mid-level like `system` and `state`, and finally to low-level workers like `agent`, `score`, and `tool`.\n",
# 420     "- **Wider bands** indicate more frequent interactions. For example, the `state → score` and `score → tool` flows are thick, indicating heavy evaluation and tool usage.\n",
# 421     "- **Branching paths** (e.g., from `agent` to `score`, `tool`, `agent_engine`) reveal the dependencies that agents rely on to make decisions.\n",
# 422     "\n",
# 423     "This diagram is useful for identifying:\n",
# 424     "- Execution bottlenecks\n",
# 425     "- Overused subsystems\n",
# 426     "- System architecture layering\n",
# 427     "\n",
# 428     "It’s a high-level snapshot of how components orchestrate a complete run.\n"
# 429    ]

# 432    "cell_type": "code",

# 434    "id": "087a0eea",
# 435    "metadata": {},
# 436    "outputs": [],
# 437    "source": [
# 438     "import plotly.graph_objects as go\n",
# 439     "\n",
# 440     "#  Step 1: Clean copy\n",
# 441     "df_sankey = df.copy()\n",
# 442     "\n",
# 443     "#  Step 2: Simplify labels to suffix\n",
# 444     "df_sankey[\"source\"] = df_sankey[\"called_by_type\"].fillna(\"start\")\n",
# 445     "df_sankey[\"target\"] = df_sankey[\"provider_type\"]\n",
# 446     "df_sankey[\"source_label\"] = df_sankey[\"source\"].apply(lambda x: str(x).split(\".\")[-1])\n",
# 447     "df_sankey[\"target_label\"] = df_sankey[\"target\"].apply(lambda x: str(x).split(\".\")[-1])\n",
# 448     "\n",
# 449     "#  Step 3: Enforce node order by appearance in time\n",
# 450     "ordered_labels = pd.concat([df_sankey[\"source_label\"], df_sankey[\"target_label\"]], ignore_index=True).dropna().unique().tolist()\n",
# 451     "node_indices = {label: i for i, label in enumerate(ordered_labels)}\n",
# 452     "\n",
# 453     "#  Step 4: Build link data\n",
# 454     "link_data = (\n",
# 455     "    df_sankey.groupby([\"source_label\", \"target_label\"])\n",
# 456     "    .size()\n",
# 457     "    .reset_index(name=\"count\")\n",
# 458     "    .assign(\n",
# 459     "        source_idx=lambda d: d[\"source_label\"].map(node_indices),\n",
# 460     "        target_idx=lambda d: d[\"target_label\"].map(node_indices)\n",
# 461     "    )\n",
# 462     ")\n",
# 463     "\n",
# 464     "#  Step 5: Plot Sankey\n",
# 465     "fig = go.Figure(go.Sankey(\n",
# 466     "    node=dict(\n",
# 467     "        pad=15,\n",
# 468     "        thickness=20,\n",
# 469     "        line=dict(color=\"black\", width=0.5),\n",
# 470     "        label=ordered_labels\n",
# 471     "    ),\n",
# 472     "    link=dict(\n",
# 473     "        source=link_data[\"source_idx\"],\n",
# 474     "        target=link_data[\"target_idx\"],\n",
# 475     "        value=link_data[\"count\"]\n",
# 476     "    )\n",
# 477     "))\n",
# 478     "\n",
# 479     "fig.update_layout(title_text=\"🧩 Execution Flow\", font_size=14)\n",
# 480     "fig.show()\n"
# 481    ]

# 747     "\n",

# 752     "fig = px.bar(\n",

# 688     "    lambda row: f\"{row['entity_layer']}: {row['from_state'].split('.')[-1]} → {row['to_state'].split('.')[-1]}\", axis=1\n",
# 689     ")\n",
# 690     "\n",
# 691     "unique_runs = df_timeline['run_id'].unique()\n",
# 692     "palette = sns.color_palette(\"husl\", len(unique_runs))\n",
# 693     "run_color_map = dict(zip(unique_runs, palette))\n",
# 694     "df_timeline['color'] = df_timeline['run_id'].map(run_color_map)\n",
# 695     "\n",
# 696     "plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))\n",
# 697     "sns.scatterplot(\n",
# 698     "    x='timestamp',\n",
# 699     "    y='label',\n",
# 700     "    data=df_timeline,\n",

# 723     "This code generates a **manual-layout node graph** using **Graphviz** to illustrate the **linear flow of state transitions** across the FSM lifecycle. Each state is visualized as a colored node, positioned in a fixed 4-column grid layout for clarity.\n",
# 724     "\n",
# 725     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 726     "\n",
# 727     "* **Prepares the data**:\n",
# 728     "\n",
# 729     "  * Extracts structured transition metadata (including file names) from the `transition_metadata` field.\n",
# 730     "  * Computes a color for each node based on its `entity_type` (e.g., `CONTROLLER`, `STATE`, `AGENT`).\n",
# 731     "\n",
# 732     "* **Constructs the graph layout**:\n",
# 733     "\n",
# 734     "  * Each node corresponds to a `to_state`, visually labeled with:\n",
# 735     "\n",
# 736     "    * The FSM state name (e.g., `PREPROCESSING`, `LINTING`)\n",
# 737     "    * The associated filename (e.g., `__ctrl_...py`)\n",
# 738     "  * Node layout is positioned manually in a fixed grid (4 nodes per row) using the `neato` engine and explicit `(x, y)` coordinates.\n",
# 739     "\n",
# 740     "* **Adds edges**:\n",
# 741     "\n",
# 742     "  * Solid arrows represent sequential transitions with labeled metadata (e.g., `ACCEPTED | AGENT`).\n",
# 743     "  * Dashed arrows mark transitions between rows to preserve visual flow (e.g., \"next ➜\").\n",
# 744     "\n",
# 745     "* **Applies styling**:\n",
# 746     "\n",
# 747     "  * Background colors are applied per provider type (e.g., AGENT = pink, SYSTEM = yellow).\n",
# 748     "  * Node labels use HTML-style formatting for bold titles and compact file references.\n",
# 749     "  * The graph includes a left-aligned title with padding (`\"File State Transition Lineage\"`).\n",
# 750     "\n",

# 1148     "\n",
# 1149     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 1150     "\n",
# 1151     "* **Prepares the data**:\n",

# 1155     "\n",

# 2233     "\n",
# 2234     "#  Step 2: Count transition reasons\n",

# 2242     "\n",
